questions.stem: A completed ordinary jurat is priced under the handbook. What ceiling is stated?
questions.explanation: The listed ordinary jurat fee is five dollars per jurat.
feedback: The act remains capped.
Correct. The listed ordinary jurat fee is five dollars per jurat.
Travel or hourly concepts do not set this act fee.
The listed maximum is lower.

questions.stem: An officer adds a technology amount for a remote act. What maximum additional remote fee does the rule describe?
options: An amount not exceeding $25 for each remote act alongside authorized fees
questions.explanation: The rule describes the additional remote fee with a twenty-five-dollar ceiling.
feedback: Correct. The rule describes the additional remote fee with a twenty-five-dollar ceiling.
The provision caps the amount.
That exceeds the stated ceiling.
Assurance is not service pricing.

questions.stem: A mobile officer first announces travel charges after arriving. What advance conditions does the handbook state?
options: Only a customer signature after departure
Agreement before travel and explanation that travel is separate and not mandated by law
questions.explanation: The handbook requires advance travel agreement and the separate nonmandatory-fee explanation.
feedback: Later billing does not provide advance agreement.
The requester must agree.
An after-the-fact signature does not follow the timing.
Correct. The handbook requires advance travel agreement and the separate nonmandatory-fee explanation.

questions.stem: An officer doubles the same act fee solely based on the principal's personal attributes. What limitation applies?
options: A journal entry automatically permits it
Do not condition fees discriminatorily on principal attributes
Any discriminatory price is allowed below the bond amount
questions.explanation: The handbook prohibits that discriminatory conditioning.
feedback: The officer also has the duty.
Recording a violation does not authorize it.
Correct. The handbook prohibits that discriminatory conditioning.
The bond does not set a pricing exemption.

questions.stem: An employer instructs the office notary to exceed the statutory act fee. What does the handbook state?
options: A larger sign creates an exception
The employer shall not establish fees above the specified schedule
Only the client can waive all caps
questions.explanation: The handbook expressly restricts employer-established excessive fees.
feedback: Advertising size does not set legality.
Correct. The handbook expressly restricts employer-established excessive fees.
Employment does not override the cap.
Consent does not erase the schedule.

questions.stem: A seller markets the notary appointment as approval of services the person cannot provide. What does the handbook prohibit?
questions.explanation: The handbook bars deceptive notarial advertising.
feedback: Correct. The handbook bars deceptive notarial advertising.
Low pricing is not the described false-authority issue.
Accurate hours are different.
Permitted service descriptions need not be deceptive.

questions.stem: A commissioned nonlawyer uses notario publico as a service title. What does the handbook state?
options: A high course score creates an exception
Do not use notario or notario publico
questions.explanation: The handbook expressly prohibits those terms.
feedback: Commissioning does not remove the prohibition.
The statement is a title restriction.
Examination performance does not confer legal-professional status.
Correct. The handbook expressly prohibits those terms.

questions.stem: An officer keeps a customer's original to pressure payment and blocks access. What does the handbook prohibit?
options: Only keeping the officer's own journal
Withholding access to or possession of the supplied original
Only giving a certified entry copy
questions.explanation: The handbook prohibits withholding the original supplied for service.
feedback: The journal is a separate official record.
An application is not the described client original.
Correct. The handbook prohibits withholding the original supplied for service.
A lawful copy service is different.

questions.stem: A client leaves essential record fields empty and asks for immediate stamping. What boundary applies?
options: Let a future stranger fill it
No notarial act on a blank or incomplete record
Proceed if the client is well known
Proceed only with a larger stamp
questions.explanation: The handbook expressly prohibits acting on blank or incomplete records.
feedback: Later uncontrolled completion is not a cure.
Correct. The handbook expressly prohibits acting on blank or incomplete records.
Identity does not cure document incompleteness.
Stamp size does not complete the record.

questions.stem: A notary intentionally alters official act evidence to deceive a recipient. What rule applies?
options: No notarial act with intent to deceive or defraud
A later journal note always cures it
questions.explanation: The handbook prohibits deceitful or fraudulent notarial conduct.
feedback: Correct. The handbook prohibits deceitful or fraudulent notarial conduct.
Payment does not legalize intent.
Workplace instructions do not create authority.
Documentation cannot erase intentional misconduct.

questions.stem: The notary personally has a direct beneficial interest in a record and completes the act anyway. What status does the statute state?
options: The act is immune from challenge
A second stamp erases the conflict
questions.explanation: The statute describes an act violating that conflict provision as voidable.
feedback: The provision permits challenge.
Payment does not remove the prohibition.
Additional impressions do not cure the interest.
Correct. The statute describes an act violating that conflict provision as voidable.

questions.stem: A notary ceases both state residence and state employment. What does the handbook direct?
options: Transfer the stamp to a friend
Notify SOS of resignation and disable the official stamp
Keep acting solely because the certificate date is future
questions.explanation: Loss of both qualifying connections triggers the described resignation steps.
feedback: Office cannot be transferred by a device.
An informal profile change is not resignation.
Correct. Loss of both qualifying connections triggers the described resignation steps.
Term dates do not restore qualification.

questions.stem: A person no longer qualifies for the automatic public office and no longer wants its duties. What state route is described?
options: Notify SOS through the automatic-officer resignation filing
Use a former office stamp forever
questions.explanation: The handbook provides online resignation for that automatic role.
feedback: Customer notice does not update the state record.
Correct. The handbook provides online resignation for that automatic role.
A separate commission has its own prerequisites.
Former office does not preserve authority.

questions.stem: Which state body does the official overview identify for adverse actions against notary commissions for misconduct?
questions.explanation: The official overview assigns the described RULONA adverse-action authority to the State Ethics Commission.
feedback: Correct. The official overview assigns the described RULONA adverse-action authority to the State Ethics Commission.
Manufacturing does not confer disciplinary power.
Training providers do not adjudicate state commissions.
Employment does not assign that public power.

questions.stem: A person wants to submit a RULONA complaint through the official current route. Which agency portal is identified?
options: The State Ethics Commission proceedings portal
questions.explanation: The agency's official page links its complaint portal.
feedback: A rating does not file the agency complaint.
Insurance commerce is separate.
An informal message is not the identified filing route.
Correct. The agency's official page links its complaint portal.

questions.stem: A Santa Fe notary has bought a RON subscription and passed its course, but SOS approval is pending. What authorizes the first remote act?
options: A customer's agreement to waive approval
Receipt of SOS authorization before performing the act
questions.explanation: The officer must receive SOS approval before remotely notarizing a record.
feedback: An ordinary commission alone does not authorize RON.
A customer cannot waive the state approval requirement.
Correct. The officer must receive SOS approval before remotely notarizing a record.
Provider payment does not issue state authority.

questions.stem: An applicant wants an ordinary commission and RON authorization together. Which filing approach does the rule permit?
options: Applying only to a RON vendor
Simultaneously applying for the commission and RON authorization
Performing remote acts first to demonstrate experience
Waiting through one full commission term
questions.explanation: An individual may simultaneously apply to be commissioned and authorized for RON.
feedback: A vendor application does not replace the SOS applications.
Correct. An individual may simultaneously apply to be commissioned and authorized for RON.
Remote acts still require prior SOS approval.
The rule does not require a completed prior term.

questions.stem: A RON applicant plans to use two SOS-approved systems. What belongs in the application?
options: The names of all approved systems the applicant intends to use
The name of a generic video-call service
No system information until the first complaint
questions.explanation: The application identifies every approved RON system the officer intends to use.
feedback: Correct. The application identifies every approved RON system the officer intends to use.
The requirement covers both intended systems.
A generic service name does not identify the intended approved systems.
System information is required with the application.

questions.stem: An applicant lists a RON provider but leaves the record-storage explanation blank. What is missing?
options: Only an estimate of the applicant's future revenue
A promise that the signer will keep all records
The signer's password for the storage account
The methods and technology for maintaining the journal, if applicable, and audiovisual recording
questions.explanation: The application must explain the methods and technology for the required journal and audiovisual storage.
feedback: Revenue projections do not explain record preservation.
Assigning everything to the signer does not satisfy the officer's application duty.
A signer's password is not the required storage explanation.
Correct. The application must explain the methods and technology for the required journal and audiovisual storage.

questions.stem: An officer budgets for a first RON authorization application. What application fee does the rule specify?
options: No fee if the provider charged tuition
A fee set independently by each signer
questions.explanation: The RON application carries a nonrefundable $75 fee, separate from training charges.
feedback: Provider tuition does not replace the application fee.
The state rule sets the application fee.
Correct. The RON application carries a nonrefundable $75 fee, separate from training charges.
The rule specifies $75 and nonrefundability.

questions.stem: A previously RON-authorized notary renews an unexpired commission. Does the rule ordinarily require another RON application?
options: No renewal of any kind is needed
The commission renewal renews the RON qualification without another RON application
Yes, a new RON application is required after every remote act
Yes, all earlier RON approvals automatically vanish each calendar year
questions.explanation: Renewal of the commission ordinarily renews the existing RON qualification without a separate application under this section.
feedback: The officer still must renew the commission.
Correct. Renewal of the commission ordinarily renews the existing RON qualification without a separate application under this section.
The rule does not require an application per act.
The rule ties this continuation to commission renewal.

questions.stem: A former RON notary's commission has been expired for eighteen months. What does the RON renewal rule require?
options: A RON authorization application and its required application fee
Automatic RON continuation based only on the old approval
Using the former electronic stamp until the next renewal
questions.explanation: A commission expired for more than one year triggers a new RON authorization application and fee.
feedback: Correct. A commission expired for more than one year triggers a new RON authorization application and fee.
The over-one-year exception prevents automatic continuation.
Provider notice does not replace the state application.
An expired commission does not support continued acts.

questions.stem: A third-party vendor administers the required New Mexico RON examination. How long must it retain the examination records, including scores?
options: Only until the applicant buys software
questions.explanation: The rule requires third-party RON examination records to be retained for five years.
feedback: A software purchase does not end the retention duty.
Thirty days is shorter than the required five years.
The first act does not terminate the vendor's record duty.
Correct. The rule requires third-party RON examination records to be retained for five years.

questions.stem: During a RON session, a person beside the signer keeps answering and the signer looks fearful. Which observation is relevant under the rule?
options: The conduct of others in the room and the signer's signs of discomfort
Only whether the file has a signature box
questions.explanation: The officer may consider both the signer's behavior and surroundings when assessing coercion.
feedback: Prepayment does not establish free will.
Connection speed alone does not address the troubling behavior.
Correct. The officer may consider both the signer's behavior and surroundings when assessing coercion.
A signature box does not resolve potential coercion.

questions.stem: After all available checks, a remote officer cannot verify the principal's identity in compliance with the rules. What follows?
options: The officer may ask the signer to waive identification
The officer must refuse to complete the act
The officer may proceed if the signature looks familiar
The officer may charge more and skip identity verification
questions.explanation: Inability to verify identity under the rules requires refusal to complete the remote act.
feedback: The signer cannot waive the officer's identification duty.
Correct. Inability to verify identity under the rules requires refusal to complete the remote act.
Signature familiarity alone cannot substitute for compliant identity verification.
A fee cannot cure an unresolved identity failure.

questions.stem: A remote officer learns that the session's communication technology is insecure. What must the officer do?
options: Refuse to complete the notarial act
Proceed because the signer already answered a quiz
Proceed if no fee is charged
Finish first and report the insecurity at renewal
questions.explanation: Awareness that communication technology is insecure requires refusal to complete the act.
feedback: Correct. Awareness that communication technology is insecure requires refusal to complete the act.
An earlier quiz does not cure insecure communication.
An unpaid act still requires secure technology.
The rule requires action during the transaction.

questions.stem: The RON platform cannot attach the principal's signature to the electronic record. Which response complies?
options: Insert the principal's name into the journal as a substitute
Treat a verbal promise as an attached signature
Complete only the certificate and ignore the record
questions.explanation: The officer must refuse when the principal's signature cannot be attached to the electronic record.
feedback: A journal entry does not attach the signature to the record.
A verbal promise does not correct the attachment failure.
A certificate alone cannot cure the identified defect.
Correct. The officer must refuse when the principal's signature cannot be attached to the electronic record.

questions.stem: The platform can display the officer's stamp but cannot make later changes to the record evident. What should the officer do?
options: Proceed because displaying the stamp is enough
Ask the signer to promise not to edit
Refuse to complete the remote act
questions.explanation: The stamp must be attached through technology that makes subsequent changes evident.
feedback: A visible image alone does not satisfy the technology requirement.
A promise does not replace tamper-evident attachment.
Correct. The stamp must be attached through technology that makes subsequent changes evident.
Stamp size does not supply tamper evidence.

questions.stem: A remote principal is not personally known to the officer and is using the standard identity-proofing route. What is required?
options: Any one question selected by the officer
Two different types of identity proofing with credential analysis, successful KBA, and visual comparison
Only an emailed photograph of a signature
Only an employer's assurance that the account is active
questions.explanation: The prescribed route combines credential analysis and knowledge-based authentication, with real-time visual comparison.
feedback: The officer cannot replace the prescribed process with one homemade question.
Correct. The prescribed route combines credential analysis and knowledge-based authentication, with real-time visual comparison.
A signature photograph does not supply the required proofing procedures.
An active account does not establish the required identity proofing.

questions.stem: A credential-analysis service merely reads the printed name without testing security features. What is missing?
options: An authenticity test using appropriate technologies and authoritative information as available
A requirement that every signer buy a new passport
A rule allowing the officer to trust any uploaded image
A requirement to store the officer's answers to identity questions
questions.explanation: Credential analysis must test genuineness, including security features, and use authoritative source information as available.
feedback: Correct. Credential analysis must test genuineness, including security features, and use authoritative source information as available.
The rule does not require every signer to buy a new passport.
An unchecked image does not provide the required authenticity analysis.
The officer's answers are unrelated to the principal's credential authenticity.

questions.stem: A provider proposes a KBA quiz with four questions and four choices per question. How must it be changed?
options: Use one question with ten choices
Keep four questions if the officer knows the address
Replace the quiz with a handwritten signature sample
Use at least five questions with at least five choices for each
questions.explanation: The KBA minimum is five questions and five possible answers to each question.
feedback: One question does not meet the minimum question count.
Knowing an address does not reduce the prescribed minimums.
A signature sample does not supply the required KBA quiz.
Correct. The KBA minimum is five questions and five possible answers to each question.

questions.stem: A remote principal takes the prescribed KBA quiz. Which success standard applies to that identity quiz?
options: The same unidentified time limit as the notary licensing examination
At least 80% correct with all answers completed within two minutes
Any correct answer within ten minutes
questions.explanation: The identity quiz requires at least 80% correct and completion within two minutes. These are identity-proofing specifications.
feedback: The rule supplies an 80% threshold and a two-minute limit.
KBA specifications do not establish the notary examination's length.
Correct. The identity quiz requires at least 80% correct and completion within two minutes. These are identity-proofing specifications.
One correct answer does not meet the percentage threshold.

questions.stem: A principal fails the KBA quiz twice. When may that person retake it under the rule?
options: After changing the account's display name
Immediately until a passing result appears
After the officer reads the answers aloud
questions.explanation: After two failed attempts the individual may not retake the quiz within 24 hours.
feedback: A display-name change does not eliminate the waiting restriction.
Correct. After two failed attempts the individual may not retake the quiz within 24 hours.
Unlimited immediate retries violate the waiting restriction.
Providing answers would defeat the prescribed identity assessment.

questions.stem: A provider prepares a permitted KBA retake. How much of the prior quiz must be replaced?
options: At least 40% of the prior questions
Exactly one answer choice across the entire quiz
No questions if the order is shuffled
questions.explanation: A retake must replace at least forty percent of the prior questions.
feedback: Correct. A retake must replace at least forty percent of the prior questions.
Changing one choice does not satisfy the question-replacement requirement.
Reordering the same questions does not replace them.
Renumbering leaves the prior questions unchanged.

questions.stem: A provider offers the officer a screen showing the principal's KBA questions and answers. Should the officer use that feature?
options: Yes, so the officer can coach the principal
Yes, if the officer promises to delete the screen later
Yes, because the answers belong in the journal
No, the officer must not be able to see or record those questions or answers
questions.explanation: The rule requires that the notarial officer cannot see or record the KBA questions or answers.
feedback: Coaching undermines the required independent assessment.
Later deletion does not cure prohibited access.
KBA answers are not a required journal field.
Correct. The rule requires that the notarial officer cannot see or record the KBA questions or answers.

questions.stem: A service sends separate prerecorded clips between a principal and an officer. Does that satisfy RON communication technology?
options: Yes, if the principal speaks clearly in one clip
Yes, if a recording is saved afterward
No, the rule requires synchronous audiovisual feeds enabling them to see and speak with each other
Yes, if each clip is shorter than one minute
questions.explanation: The technology must provide synchronous audio-video communication with sufficient clarity and resolution.
feedback: Clear prerecorded speech does not supply a live exchange.
Saving clips does not replace the synchronous session.
Correct. The technology must provide synchronous audio-video communication with sufficient clarity and resolution.
Clip length does not create simultaneous communication.

questions.stem: A remote signer has a hearing impairment. What capability must the communication technology provide?
options: Permission to replace the session with postal correspondence
Automatic rejection of every signer with a hearing impairment
questions.explanation: RON technology must provide accessibility accommodations for vision, hearing, or speech impairments.
feedback: Postal correspondence does not provide the required remote session.
Correct. RON technology must provide accessibility accommodations for vision, hearing, or speech impairments.
The rule requires accommodations rather than automatic exclusion.
Accommodations do not remove the appearance requirement.

questions.stem: A platform secures its video stream but leaves the identity-proofing process and electronic record openly accessible. Is its security scope sufficient?
options: No, reasonable safeguards must also protect identity proofing and the electronic record
Yes, because only the live video matters
Yes, if the signer consented to public access
Yes, if the notary pays for a premium account
questions.explanation: Security measures must cover the live feeds, identity-proofing methods, and the electronic record.
feedback: Correct. Security measures must cover the live feeds, identity-proofing methods, and the electronic record.
The rule expressly covers more than the video feed.
Consent does not replace the prescribed security measures.
An account's price does not establish the required protections.

questions.stem: A principal exits the RON system before the act is complete and returns minutes later. How must the officer handle the process?
options: Resume only at the stamp button
Assume the original session remained continuous
Ask an assistant to finish without the principal
Stop and restart the process from the beginning
questions.explanation: An exit before completion requires stopping and restarting the remote notarization from the beginning.
feedback: Resuming only at the final button does not restart the process.
Leaving the system triggers the rule even if the return is quick.
An assistant cannot replace the required principal's appearance.
Correct. An exit before completion requires stopping and restarting the remote notarization from the beginning.

questions.stem: The audio feed drops during a remote act. The video later returns at such poor quality that the officer believes the process is compromised. What does the rule require?
options: Turn off recording and continue by text
Ignore the interruption if the fee was collected
Stop and restart the process from the beginning
Complete the certificate using the earlier clear minutes
questions.explanation: Interrupted feeds and compromised transmission quality each require restarting the process.
feedback: Text-only completion does not cure the failed audiovisual process.
Fee collection does not excuse the technology requirement.
Correct. Interrupted feeds and compromised transmission quality each require restarting the process.
Earlier clear communication does not remove the restart requirement.

questions.stem: An officer evaluates a digital certificate for RON. Which technical standard does the rule identify?
options: A certificate that expired yesterday but still opens
A valid third-party PKI certificate compliant with X.509 or higher
Any image file containing a drawn signature
questions.explanation: The selected technology must use a valid third-party PKI digital certificate compliant with X.509 or higher.
feedback: An expired certificate may not be used for an electronic act.
Correct. The selected technology must use a valid third-party PKI digital certificate compliant with X.509 or higher.
A signature image is not the required digital certificate.
A protected document does not supply the specified certificate.

questions.stem: A manager wants the employee-notary's RON password so coworkers can apply the electronic stamp during lunch. What rule controls?
options: The electronic signature and stamp remain under the officer's sole control and access
The employer may share access because it paid the invoice
Any trained coworker may use the stamp
Sharing is permitted if the manager keeps a list
questions.explanation: The officer retains sole control and access, and the employer must not allow anyone else to use the credentials.
feedback: Correct. The officer retains sole control and access, and the employer must not allow anyone else to use the credentials.
Paying the invoice does not transfer the officer's authority.
Coworker training does not permit use of another officer's signature or stamp.
A usage list does not cure unauthorized sharing.

questions.stem: A RON provider advertises that New Mexico SOS mandates purchase of its premium service. What regulatory risk does that claim create?
options: The statement automatically extends every notary's commission
The provider may charge any notarial fee it chooses
The advertisement replaces individual RON approval
The SOS may terminate the provider's active approval for that representation
questions.explanation: Representing that SOS endorses, recommends, or mandates a provider's goods or services is a ground for terminating approval.
feedback: Provider advertising does not change commission terms.
The claim does not remove fee limits.
A provider's advertisement does not authorize an individual officer.
Correct. Representing that SOS endorses, recommends, or mandates a provider's goods or services is a ground for terminating approval.

questions.stem: An active RON provider ignores an SOS investigation request for information for more than ten business days. What consequence does the rule authorize?
options: Transfer of the officer's commission to the provider
Termination of the provider's active approval
questions.explanation: Failure to respond within ten business days or cooperate with an investigation is a listed termination ground.
feedback: A provider cannot acquire an officer's commission through nonresponse.
The failure does not create a storage exemption.
Correct. Failure to respond within ten business days or cooperate with an investigation is a listed termination ground.
Ignoring an investigation does not secure renewal.

questions.stem: A noncommissioned notarial officer wants to conduct RON because the officer already has authority for traditional acts. What is required?
options: Treat official employment as a blanket RON exemption
Follow the RON authorization application procedures and comply with the RON rules upon approval
Use a commissioned coworker's remote credentials
questions.explanation: Noncommissioned notarial officers must apply under the same authorization procedures and comply with applicable remote-act requirements.
feedback: Official status does not create the claimed exemption.
Correct. Noncommissioned notarial officers must apply under the same authorization procedures and comply with applicable remote-act requirements.
Traditional authority does not eliminate the RON application.
The officer cannot use another person's remote credentials.

cards.title: Qualification route
cards.front: What connection to New Mexico supports an ordinary application?
cards.rule: An applicant must reside in New Mexico or have a place of employment in New Mexico.
cards.boundary: Age eighteen and ability to read and write English remain separate qualifications.
cards.mixup: A workplace connection does not waive the other qualifications.

cards.title: Matching legal identity
cards.front: How should the applicant's name be presented?
cards.rule: The application uses the name on the applicant's state-issued identification, with matching names and signatures on the application and bond.
cards.boundary: Review the documents before submitting the application.
cards.mixup: A preferred business nickname does not cure inconsistent application documents.

cards.title: Assurance before issuance
cards.front: What bond belongs in the ordinary application?
cards.rule: The applicant supplies a $10,000 surety bond or functional equivalent from an authorized issuer covering the commission term.
cards.boundary: The oath and assurance precede issuance.
cards.mixup: The bond does not itself issue a commission.

cards.title: Ordinary application fee
cards.front: What does the ordinary application fee cover?
cards.rule: The ordinary application requires a nonrefundable $30 application fee.
cards.boundary: Training and examination charges are separate.
cards.mixup: Paying tuition does not pay the state application fee.

cards.title: Official status boundary
cards.front: Does an attorney's notarial authority remove preparation duties?
cards.rule: A New Mexico licensed attorney acting as an automatic notarial officer must complete required training and register the official stamp before performing acts.
cards.boundary: The automatic-officer route has its own title and stamp identifiers.
cards.mixup: Holding a professional license does not eliminate the notarial preparation requirements.
cards.source: 14-14A-9 NMSA, as amended by 2023 Chapter110; handbook Automatic Notarial Officers

cards.title: Ordinary examination threshold
cards.front: What score establishes passage of the ordinary required examination?
cards.rule: An applicant must provide proof of passing the approved examination with a score of at least eighty percent.
cards.boundary: The reviewed official materials do not establish an examination question count or time allowance.
cards.mixup: An identity-proofing quiz's two-minute limit is a different specification.

cards.title: Renewal training exception
cards.front: When can a prior passing result support renewal?
cards.rule: A recorded prior passing result ordinarily permits a renewal training and examination exemption unless the commission expired more than one year or SOS determines substantial law or rule changes require retraining.
cards.boundary: Confirm that SOS has the prior passing record.
cards.mixup: A short expiration alone does not resolve the substantial-change exception.

cards.title: Evidence of completion
cards.front: What should the applicant preserve after approved training?
cards.rule: The applicant needs proof of successful approved training and examination to accompany the required application.
cards.boundary: A vendor's attendance acknowledgment may differ from proof of passage.
cards.mixup: Completing payment does not establish a passing score.

cards.title: Vendor examination records
cards.front: How long must an approved ordinary exam vendor keep examination records?
cards.rule: The third-party vendor must retain examination records, including the applicant's score, for five years.
cards.boundary: This vendor duty differs from the officer's ten-year journal retention.
cards.mixup: Issuance of a commission does not immediately end vendor retention.

cards.title: RON examination is separate
cards.front: What examination accompanies RON qualification?
cards.rule: RON authorization requires the approved remote-notarization course and examination, with proof of a score of at least eighty percent.
cards.boundary: The RON training fee is separate from the RON application fee.
cards.mixup: Passing ordinary training does not automatically grant remote authority.

cards.title: Oath before issuance
cards.front: When does the applicant take the oath of office?
cards.rule: The applicant takes the required oath before the commission is issued.
cards.boundary: The oath is part of preparing a complete application.
cards.mixup: An issued bond does not stand in for the applicant's oath.

cards.title: Another current officer
cards.front: Who notarizes the applicant's oath?
cards.rule: Another currently authorized New Mexico notarial officer notarizes the applicant's oath of office.
cards.boundary: An applicant who already has a commission still cannot notarize the applicant's own signature.
cards.mixup: Renewal does not create a self-notarization exception.
cards.source: SOS Become a Notary, oath instructions; 12.9.3.8(A)(3) NMAC

cards.title: Bond signature
cards.front: Who notarizes the applicant's principal signature on the bond?
cards.rule: Another currently commissioned New Mexico notary notarizes the applicant's principal signature on the bond.
cards.boundary: Check the bond's required names and signatures against the application.
cards.mixup: A surety's issuance alone does not replace the principal-signature notarization.
cards.source: SOS Become a Notary, Acknowledgment of Principal; 12.9.3.8(A)(2) NMAC

cards.title: Office begins with commission
cards.front: May an applicant act immediately after taking the oath?
cards.rule: The applicant must receive the commission and satisfy pre-act stamp registration before performing ordinary notarial acts.
cards.boundary: Taking the oath is an application prerequisite.
cards.mixup: An oath form is not a temporary commission.

cards.title: Renewal preparation
cards.front: How should an existing officer handle a renewal oath?
cards.rule: A renewal applicant arranges for another current New Mexico officer to notarize the required oath.
cards.boundary: The applicant's active commission does not permit notarizing the applicant's own signature.
cards.mixup: An unexpired personal stamp does not authorize a self-administered notarization.
cards.source: SOS Become a Notary, oath instructions; 12.9.3.8(A)(3) NMAC

cards.title: Commissioned stamp identity
cards.front: Which identifying details belong on a commissioned notary's stamp?
cards.rule: The stamp includes the commissioned legal name, commission number, expiration date, and required New Mexico designation and official seal.
cards.boundary: The name must match the commission.
cards.mixup: A company logo does not replace the official identifiers.

cards.title: Legible official wording
cards.front: What type size applies to the official stamp?
cards.rule: The official stamp must use ten-point type under the New Mexico rule.
cards.boundary: Commissioned and automatic officers use their applicable titles and identifiers.
cards.mixup: A supplier's decorative design does not override the ten-point requirement.

cards.title: Permanent reproduction
cards.front: What physical quality must the traditional stamp have?
cards.rule: The stamp uses permanent ink and can be reproduced under photographic methods.
cards.boundary: Check the impression for legibility on the completed record.
cards.mixup: An attractive impression that cannot be reproduced is insufficient.

cards.title: Attorney identifier
cards.front: What special identifier appears on an automatic attorney officer's stamp?
cards.rule: The automatic attorney notarial officer's stamp includes the attorney's state bar identification number.
cards.boundary: The applicable automatic-officer stamp requirements remain required.
cards.mixup: An ordinary commission number is not the attorney-role identifier.

cards.title: Judicial jurisdiction
cards.front: What geographical identifier applies to a judicial automatic officer?
cards.rule: A judicial officer's official stamp identifies the applicable judicial district or area served.
cards.boundary: Use the current statute for the judicial-role distinction.
cards.mixup: The county-clerk stamp rule does not determine the judicial stamp's jurisdiction wording.

cards.title: First-act condition
cards.front: May a new notary use the stamp during the forty-five-day filing window?
cards.rule: The official stamp copy must be provided to SOS within forty-five days and before the first notarial act.
cards.boundary: Both conditions apply.
cards.mixup: The outer filing deadline does not allow earlier unregistered acts.

cards.title: Replacement registration
cards.front: What happens after obtaining a replacement official stamp?
cards.rule: The officer follows the SOS stamp-registration process for the replacement stamp.
cards.boundary: Protect the replacement from unauthorized use.
cards.mixup: Purchasing a replacement does not update the state's stamp record.
cards.source: SOS Handbook, Changes and Stamp Requirements

cards.title: Name amendment
cards.front: What follows an approved change of commissioned name?
cards.rule: The officer obtains the amended commission and a stamp reflecting the new commissioned name and registers the updated stamp.
cards.boundary: The legal identity on the stamp must match the amended commission.
cards.mixup: A handwritten correction on the old stamp impression does not update the commission.

cards.title: Electronic stamp receipt
cards.front: What is required before the first RON act?
cards.rule: SOS must receive the electronic stamp copy before the first RON, and the copy is due within forty-five days of authorization.
cards.boundary: Remote authorization and stamp submission are separate steps.
cards.mixup: An ordinary ink-stamp filing does not supply the electronic-stamp copy.

cards.title: No public stamp sharing
cards.front: May an officer publish an official stamp image for general use?
cards.rule: The officer must not share or publish the official stamp for others to use.
cards.boundary: Required submission to SOS serves the official registration process.
cards.mixup: A business website is not the official registration channel.

cards.title: Journal duration
cards.front: How long does the officer retain the journal?
cards.rule: The journal is retained for ten years after the last notarial act recorded in it, unless transferred as authorized.
cards.boundary: Expiration or resignation does not erase retention duties.
cards.mixup: Counting from the journal's purchase date can shorten the required period.

cards.title: Authorized transfer
cards.front: What notice accompanies a journal transfer to the state records officer?
cards.rule: The officer notifies SOS on the prescribed form within thirty days of transferring the journal to the state records officer.
cards.boundary: Use an authorized recipient and retain accurate custody information.
cards.mixup: Handing the journal to a former employer does not follow this transfer procedure.

cards.title: Electronic recovery
cards.front: What resilience must an electronic journal provide?
cards.rule: The electronic journal must be permanent, tamper-evident, and recoverable after a hardware or software failure.
cards.boundary: Entries must be producible in PDF as required by the rule.
cards.mixup: An editable spreadsheet with no recovery plan does not meet these standards.

cards.title: RON recording storage
cards.front: What recording-storage qualities does New Mexico prescribe?
cards.rule: RON recordings use an open file format and protection against unauthorized access by password or cryptographic process.
cards.boundary: The recording must not include images of the record being notarized.
cards.mixup: Saving a document screen capture into the recording conflicts with the specific restriction.

cards.title: Repository exit
cards.front: What should the RON repository contract address when service ends?
cards.rule: The written contract must support continuing retention and the required control, copies, or secure return of recordings after termination.
cards.boundary: Review the exit terms before relying on a provider.
cards.mixup: Canceling a subscription does not end the statutory recording-retention obligation.

cards.title: Sworn verification
cards.front: What distinguishes a verification on oath or affirmation?
cards.rule: The principal declares the statement's truth under oath or affirmation before the officer, with identity established and the signature made in the officer's presence.
cards.boundary: A preexisting signature alone does not supply the required present signing.
cards.mixup: Acknowledging execution does not supply a sworn declaration of truth.

cards.title: Acknowledgment declaration
cards.front: What does a representative acknowledge?
cards.rule: The individual declares execution for the record's stated purpose and, in a representative capacity, proper authority and execution as the represented person's act.
cards.boundary: Identify the individual appearing.
cards.mixup: A representative acknowledgment does not establish the underlying facts as sworn testimony.

cards.title: Recent expired identification
cards.front: How recent may an otherwise acceptable expired credential be?
cards.rule: The statute permits the listed identity credential if current or expired no more than one year before the act.
cards.boundary: The credential must otherwise satisfy the statutory category and identification requirements.
cards.mixup: Another state's longer expired-ID window does not govern New Mexico acts.

cards.title: Directed signature helper
cards.front: Who may sign when the principal is physically unable?
cards.rule: The principal may direct someone other than the notarial officer to sign, and the officer records the required directed-signature notation.
cards.boundary: The principal's direction remains essential.
cards.mixup: The officer cannot become the directed signer in the officer's own act.

cards.title: Neutral refusal
cards.front: What concerns can justify refusing an act?
cards.rule: The officer may refuse when the principal's capacity or knowing and voluntary action is in doubt, subject to applicable nondiscrimination requirements.
cards.boundary: Consider the actual circumstances of the requested act.
cards.mixup: Discrimination in refusing or performing the act is prohibited.

cards.title: Original eligible record
cards.front: Which originals are excluded by the handbook's copy-certification instruction?
cards.rule: The original must not be a vital record, public record, or publicly recordable document.
cards.boundary: Direct the customer to the appropriate custodian for those records.
cards.mixup: A customer's permission does not expand the handbook's copy-certification scope.

cards.title: Comparison required
cards.front: How can the officer establish that a copy is accurate?
cards.rule: The officer makes or supervises the copy or reviews the original and copy to establish accuracy and completeness.
cards.boundary: Access to the original matters.
cards.mixup: A customer's statement that a copy is correct does not perform the officer's comparison.

cards.title: Copy fee minimum
cards.front: How is the ordinary copy-certification fee ceiling calculated?
cards.rule: The maximum is fifty cents per page with a minimum total charge of five dollars.
cards.boundary: Apply the special copy provision to the page count.
cards.mixup: A separate five-dollar charge for every page is not the stated copy-fee formula.

cards.title: Electronic to tangible
cards.front: Can an officer certify a tangible copy of an electronic record?
cards.rule: The statute authorizes certifying that a tangible copy is an accurate copy of an electronic record.
cards.boundary: Use the appropriate certificate and make the required accuracy determination.
cards.mixup: Printing alone does not certify the copy.

cards.title: Certified tangible original
cards.front: How does the remote rule treat a certified tangible copy of an electronic record?
cards.rule: A certified tangible copy with the required copy certificate is considered an original record under the rule.
cards.boundary: The short form for copy certification remains required.
cards.mixup: An uncertified printout does not acquire that status merely by coming from a RON platform.

cards.title: Officer location
cards.front: Where must the officer be during a New Mexico RON?
cards.rule: The authorized officer must be physically in New Mexico when the remote act occurs.
cards.boundary: The principal appears through compliant communication technology.
cards.mixup: A New Mexico commission does not authorize performing a New Mexico RON while the officer is physically elsewhere.

cards.title: Active provider each time
cards.front: When does the officer verify the provider's SOS status?
cards.rule: The officer verifies active SOS status before using the provider for each remote notarization.
cards.boundary: A provider's status can change after initial enrollment.
cards.mixup: An old screenshot does not replace the per-act check.

cards.title: KBA boundaries
cards.front: Who may see the principal's knowledge-based authentication answers?
cards.rule: The notarial officer must not be able to see or record the KBA questions or answers.
cards.boundary: The provider must implement the prescribed independent identity process.
cards.mixup: Coaching the signer through visible answers defeats the required restriction.

cards.title: Restart conditions
cards.front: What follows a broken audiovisual feed or an early system exit?
cards.rule: The officer stops and restarts the RON process from the beginning.
cards.boundary: Compromised transmission quality also triggers restarting.
cards.mixup: Resuming only at the final stamp step is insufficient.

cards.title: RON certificate disclosure
cards.front: What extra disclosure belongs in the RON certificate?
cards.rule: The electronic certificate clearly states that the principal appeared using communication technology.
cards.boundary: The ordinary certificate requirements also apply.
cards.mixup: An internal journal notation alone does not place the disclosure in the certificate.

cards.title: Prompt journal report
cards.front: What follows discovering a stolen journal?
cards.rule: The officer promptly notifies SOS on the prescribed form when the journal is lost or stolen.
cards.boundary: Prompt notice applies when the journal is lost or stolen.
cards.mixup: Waiting until the next renewal does not meet a prompt-notice requirement.

cards.title: Lost stamping device
cards.front: What follows a missing official stamping device?
cards.rule: The officer promptly notifies SOS after discovering the device is lost or stolen.
cards.boundary: The replacement stamp must follow applicable registration requirements.
cards.mixup: A planned replacement purchase does not remove the reporting duty.

cards.title: Sole custody
cards.front: Who controls the journal while the officer works for an employer?
cards.rule: The officer keeps the journal secure under the officer's control.
cards.boundary: The employer may receive clearly marked copies of relevant entries as allowed by the statute.
cards.mixup: Employment does not transfer the original journal to the employer.

cards.title: Electronic unavailability
cards.front: Does a failed electronic journal require action if its hardware still exists?
cards.rule: The electronic journal must be recoverable after a software malfunction or computer crash.
cards.boundary: Use the recovery arrangement when journal entries become inaccessible.
cards.mixup: Possessing a broken device does not make inaccessible entries available.

cards.title: Disposition after death
cards.front: Who handles the journal after an officer dies?
cards.rule: A personal representative or other person knowingly holding the journal transfers it to SOS, the state records officer, or an approved repository as authorized.
cards.boundary: The officer's death does not make the journal ordinary disposable property.
cards.mixup: Discarding the journal with household papers defeats the required disposition.

initial-process.summary: Prepare the ordinary application around eligibility, matching documents, approved learning, the oath, and assurance. A complete filing starts the state review, while commission issuance and stamp registration establish the conditions for beginning acts.

sections.heading: Eligibility and evidence
sections.body: Check age eighteen, a New Mexico residence or place of employment, and the ability to read and write English against the SOS application instructions. Review the applicable criminal-history and prior-notary disciplinary questions rather than treating training as the only qualification. Use the name appearing on state-issued identification. The application and bond require consistent names and signatures.

sections.heading: Submission and the start of authority
sections.body: Complete the approved course and examination, arrange the oath and $10,000 assurance, and upload the required evidence through the current online process. The $30 application fee is nonrefundable and does not include tuition. After issuance, obtain the compliant stamp and submit its copy within forty-five days and before performing any act. A filing receipt or course certificate does not issue a commission.

example.heading: An employee moves to Albuquerque
example.body: A person living across the state line has a place of employment in Albuquerque and applies through that connection. The person still completes the training, oath, bond, fee, and eligibility review. On receiving the commission, the person waits to perform an office acknowledgment until the stamp-copy requirement has been satisfied.

keyFacts: A residence or place of employment in New Mexico supplies the geographical connection.
The ordinary bond or equivalent assurance is $10,000.
The $30 application fee is separate from approved training charges.
Stamp registration is required before the first act.

passing-score.summary: New Mexico specifies an eighty-percent threshold for the approved ordinary examination and separately for the RON examination. Keep those specifications distinct from the timed knowledge-based authentication used to identify a remote principal.

sections.heading: Completion evidence and unknown specifications
sections.body: The application includes proof of successful approved learning and examination. Third-party examination vendors retain examination records, including scores, for five years. The official provisions reviewed establish the passing threshold. They do not establish a licensing-exam question count or time allowance, so preparation materials should leave those specifications unknown.

sections.heading: Renewal and changed rules
sections.body: Where SOS has a record of prior passage, the renewal exemption has conditions. A commission expired more than one year requires the specified learning again. Substantial statutory or rule changes, as determined by SOS, can also require retraining and reexamination. The handbook additionally describes the post-January 1, 2022 course context. Review current renewal instructions and the administrative rule together.

example.heading: A recorded passing result meets a changed-law notice
example.body: A renewing notary has a recorded prior passing score and an unexpired commission. If SOS determines that substantial changes require fresh training and examination, the notary follows that requirement. The short expiration exception alone does not answer the changed-law issue.

keyFacts: The ordinary examination passing threshold is at least eighty percent.
RON has its own approved learning and examination requirement.
Vendor examination records are retained for five years.
The reviewed materials leave licensing-exam length and duration unconfirmed.

applicant-oath.summary: The applicant's oath is an office-entry requirement performed before another authorized officer. It is separate from the oaths or affirmations the future notary may administer to customers.

sections.heading: Arrange an independent notarization
sections.body: Before issuance, the applicant takes the prescribed oath of office. Another currently authorized New Mexico notarial officer performs its notarization. The applicant's principal signature on the bond is notarized by another currently commissioned New Mexico notary. An applicant who already holds a commission cannot notarize the applicant's own signature merely because this is a renewal.

sections.heading: Complete the application sequence
sections.body: Check that the oath and bond signatures and names agree with the application requirements. Upload the required documents with the evidence of approved learning and payment through the current filing process. Taking the oath does not create interim authority. Issuance, the commission's effective period, and the stamp-copy condition still govern when ordinary acts can begin.

example.heading: A current notary renews
example.body: An active notary prepares a renewal oath and bond. A coworker who is a current authorized New Mexico officer notarizes the oath, and another current New Mexico notary notarizes the required bond signature. The applicant does not use the applicant's own stamp on either personal signature.

keyFacts: The oath precedes commission issuance.
An applicant cannot notarize the applicant's own signature.
The bond's principal signature has its own notarization requirement.
A completed oath form does not grant temporary authority.

stamp-content.summary: A New Mexico official stamp identifies the particular officer and role. Commissioned notaries and automatic notarial officers use the details applicable to their authority, including the current official-seal requirement.

sections.heading: Commissioned notary stamp
sections.body: Use the commissioned legal name, commission number, expiration date, required Notary Public and State of New Mexico wording, and the official state seal. The administrative rule requires ten-point type. The stamp must use permanent ink that is photographically reproducible. Review an impression before submitting the copy and before placing it on customer records.

sections.heading: Automatic officers and custody
sections.body: An automatic notarial officer uses the applicable Notarial Officer title and role-specific identifiers. An attorney uses the state bar identification number. Judicial officers identify the judicial district or area served, while county clerks use the applicable county detail. Follow the current statute for those distinctions. Protect the stamping device from another person's use and avoid publishing a reusable official-stamp image.

example.heading: An attorney orders the wrong design
example.body: A New Mexico attorney exercising automatic notarial authority receives a design labeled with an ordinary commission number but omitting the attorney's bar identifier. The attorney obtains a design meeting the automatic-officer requirements and registers the proper stamp before acting.

keyFacts: The commissioned name must match the commission.
The official stamp uses ten-point type.
Current law requires the official seal.
Automatic-role identifiers differ by the officer's source of authority.

stamp-registration.summary: The forty-five-day stamp requirement also contains a first-act condition. Completing the deadline calculation alone does not establish permission to start notarizing.

sections.heading: Ordinary stamp copy
sections.body: After issuance, the officer provides the official stamp copy on the prescribed SOS form within forty-five days and before performing the first notarial act. A new officer should build that filing into the start-up sequence. The rule provides for referral to the State Ethics Commission when the required information is not supplied.

sections.heading: Updates and electronic stamps
sections.body: Follow the stamp-registration process after replacement or an amended commissioned name. A name amendment requires a matching updated stamp. Remote authorization has a parallel but expressly stated electronic-stamp requirement. SOS must receive the electronic copy before the first RON and within forty-five days of authorization. The ink-stamp record does not itself provide the electronic-stamp copy.

example.heading: An act is offered on day ten
example.body: A newly commissioned notary owns a compliant stamp but has not provided the stamp copy. A customer offers an acknowledgment ten days after commissioning. The notary completes the required stamp filing before performing the act, even though the outer forty-five-day deadline has not arrived.

keyFacts: Both the forty-five-day deadline and first-act condition apply.
Electronic stamp submission accompanies remote authorization.
The RON copy must reach SOS before the first remote act.
Replacement and name changes require attention to the registered stamp.

retention.summary: A New Mexico journal supports a durable, sequential record of the officer's acts. Plan for ordinary storage, electronic recovery, departure from employment, and the end of the commission before a custody problem develops.

sections.heading: Journal format and custody
sections.body: Record each act contemporaneously with the required date and time, record and act description, principal details, identification basis, and fee if any. A tangible journal is bound with numbered pages. An electronic journal must be permanent, tamper-evident, recoverable, and producible in the required PDF form. Current statute permits a paper journal for tangible records and an electronic journal for electronic records. The officer maintains secure control. Permitted employer copies are marked as copies.

sections.heading: Ten-year duties and remote records
sections.body: Retain the journal for ten years after its last recorded act or transfer it to an authorized recipient. Resignation and suspension do not erase the duty. A transfer to the state records officer requires the prescribed SOS notice within thirty days. RON also creates a recording obligation, generally at least ten years from recording, alongside the journal. Use protected open-format recordings and a repository contract that preserves compliance when service ends.

example.heading: Leaving a law office
example.body: A notary changes employers with seven years remaining on the journal's retention period. The officer keeps or lawfully transfers the original journal and may furnish permitted, clearly marked copies of relevant entries. The employer's payment for the book does not decide custody.

keyFacts: Journal retention runs ten years from the last recorded act.
Electronic journal design includes recovery and PDF production.
RON recordings and journals are separate records.
Subscription termination does not end retention requirements.

oath.summary: Choose and perform the act that the principal's record requires. An acknowledgment concerns execution, a verification concerns sworn truth, and signature witnessing has its own presence and identity requirements.

sections.heading: Appearance and the declaration
sections.body: For a verification on oath or affirmation, establish identity, administer the truth declaration, and have the principal sign in the officer's presence. For an acknowledgment, obtain the required execution declaration, including proper authority for representative execution. Do not treat an existing signature as a substitute for a required current signing. Use the actual act date in the certificate.

sections.heading: Identity, assistance, and impartial judgment
sections.body: The listed identification may be current or expired no more than one year, subject to the statutory credential requirements. A credible witness must satisfy the statute's independence and identification conditions and give an oath or affirmation. A principal unable to sign may direct someone other than the officer to sign, with the required notation. Evaluate knowing, voluntary action and capacity concerns while following the nondiscrimination requirements.

example.heading: A signed verification arrives
example.body: A customer presents a statement signed at home and requests a verification on oath or affirmation. The officer establishes identity, administers the truth declaration, and obtains signing in the officer's presence. The officer does not convert the earlier signature into a jurat merely by adding a stamp.

keyFacts: A sworn verification requires the principal's oath or affirmation of truth.
The New Mexico expired-credential window is no more than one year.
A directed-signature helper must be someone other than the officer.
Conflicts involving the officer, spouse, or domestic partner require attention under the statute.

copy-limits.summary: Copy certification requires an accuracy determination about an eligible original. The customer's willingness to sign a statement does not replace the officer's comparison or overcome a record-type restriction.

sections.heading: Check the original and comparison method
sections.body: The handbook excludes vital records, public records, and publicly recordable documents from its ordinary copy-certification instruction. For an eligible record, the officer makes or supervises the copy or reviews the original and copy to determine completeness and accuracy. Inspect every relevant page and confirm that the certificate describes the copy and source correctly.

sections.heading: Electronic sources and fees
sections.body: Current law permits certifying that a tangible copy accurately reproduces an electronic record. Under the remote rule, a certified tangible copy of an electronic record with the required copy certificate is considered an original record. An uncertified printout does not obtain that status automatically. The ordinary copy-fee provision is fifty cents per page with a five-dollar minimum total charge. Keep copy certification distinct from authenticating a photograph, which the handbook prohibits.

example.heading: A family requests a birth-certificate copy
example.body: A customer brings a birth certificate and asks the officer to certify a photocopy. The officer identifies the vital-record restriction and refers the customer to the appropriate official custodian. A separate personal business document may be eligible after comparison with its original.

keyFacts: Review the original and complete copy.
The handbook restricts vital, public, and publicly recordable originals.
A certified tangible electronic-record copy requires the appropriate certificate.
The ordinary copy fee has a fifty-cent-per-page formula and five-dollar minimum.

separate-authorization.summary: RON requires individual state authorization, an approved active system, compliant remote appearance, and tamper-evident execution. Ordinary commissioning supplies the foundation for a commissioned applicant but does not supply remote authority by itself.

sections.heading: Apply and verify the platform
sections.body: Apply to SOS and receive approval before the first remote act. The rule permits simultaneous ordinary-commission and RON applications. Identify every approved intended system, explain journal and recording storage, supply the required training proof, and pay the nonrefundable $75 application fee. The officer must be physically in New Mexico and verify provider active status for each act. Notify SOS when adopting a new system.

sections.heading: Conduct a compliant session
sections.body: Identify the principal at the start. Where the prescribed proofing route applies, credential analysis and KBA support real-time visual comparison. KBA has its own question, timing, retry, and confidentiality rules. Use sufficient synchronous audio and video with accessibility and security protections. Restart from the beginning after exits or interrupted or compromised feeds. Maintain sole control of electronic credentials and include the communication-technology disclosure in the certificate.

example.heading: An authorized officer travels
example.body: A RON-authorized New Mexico notary visits another state and receives an urgent platform request. The officer cannot perform that New Mexico RON while physically outside New Mexico. After returning, the officer checks provider active status and other per-act requirements before accepting a new session.

keyFacts: SOS approval precedes remote acts.
The officer is physically in New Mexico during RON.
Provider active status is checked for each remote notarization.
RON electronic credentials remain under the officer's sole control.

lost-journal.summary: Loss reporting, recovery, and long-term custody work together. A journal or stamp becoming unavailable requires prompt action even when the officer plans to buy a replacement.

sections.heading: Prompt notice and secure recovery
sections.body: Promptly notify SOS on its prescribed form when the journal is lost or stolen. Prompt notice also applies to a lost or stolen stamping device. Electronic journals must be designed for recovery after software or hardware failure. Activate that recovery capability when entries become inaccessible, secure the remaining records and credentials, and follow the prescribed replacement and registration processes.

sections.heading: Departure, death, and closing the office
sections.body: Keep the original journal under the required custody when employment ends, or transfer it as the statute permits. Resignation or suspension requires continuing retention and notice of location. After death or adjudicated incompetence, the personal representative or another person knowingly possessing the journal follows the authorized disposition procedure. A stamping device must be rendered unusable when the applicable cessation rules require it.

example.heading: A laptop becomes inaccessible
example.body: A notary's electronic journal cannot be accessed after a storage failure. The officer activates the required recovery arrangement. If the journal is lost or stolen, the officer promptly follows the prescribed SOS notice process. Keeping the failed laptop physically on the desk does not supply accessible entries or the required recovery capability.

keyFacts: Prompt notice applies to lost or stolen journals and stamping devices.
Electronic journal recovery is a design requirement.
Former employers do not automatically acquire the original journal.
Death and cessation require deliberate record and device disposition.

articles.intent: Learn how New Mexico rules apply to a concrete notarial workflow
articles.title: Choosing the Act in a New Mexico Signing
articles.description: Distinguish execution declarations, sworn truth, and signature witnessing in a New Mexico transaction.
articles.h1: Choosing the Act in a New Mexico Signing
articles.lede: A signature line and a stamp box do not tell the whole story. Identify the requested act before deciding which declarations and signing steps are necessary.

sections.heading: Execution has its own declaration
sections.body: At a Las Cruces business closing, a representative brings a previously signed authorization. An acknowledgment requires identifying the individual and obtaining the declaration that execution served the record's stated purpose. For representative execution, the declaration also addresses proper authority and execution as the represented person's act. The officer's certificate records that acknowledgment. It does not establish that every factual assertion in the authorization is true.

sections.heading: A verification requires sworn truth
sections.body: A different customer brings a factual statement requiring verification on oath or affirmation. The officer must obtain the principal's declaration of truth and the signature in the officer's presence. A signature placed on the document at home does not fulfill that present-signing requirement. Arrange the required signing and declaration before completing the verification certificate. A customer who declines to make the truth declaration has left an essential part of the requested act incomplete.

sections.heading: Witnessing and directed signatures
sections.body: Signature witnessing also requires identifying the person and witnessing the signature. It does not acquire a sworn-truth declaration merely because the signature appears beside an official stamp. If a principal is physically unable to sign, the statute permits a directed signature by someone other than the officer. The officer includes the required notation identifying the directed signer and the principal. Physical assistance therefore requires its own lawful procedure.

sections.heading: Complete the actual event
sections.body: Use the actual act date and the certificate appropriate to what occurred. For an ordinary tangible transaction, the principal appears physically before the officer. The principal's requested result does not permit backdating an acknowledgment or recording an oath that was never administered. If the record is incomplete or the principal has not decided what act is required, resolve the missing instructions within the officer's lawful role before completing the certificate.

faqs.q: Can an acknowledgment prove a statement's truth?
faqs.a: An acknowledgment records the execution declaration. A verification on oath or affirmation requires a declaration of truth.

faqs.q: May the officer be the directed signer?
faqs.a: No. The directed signer must be someone other than the notarial officer.

articles.intent: Learn how New Mexico rules apply to a concrete notarial workflow
articles.title: Identity Decisions Beyond a Familiar Signature
articles.description: Apply New Mexico's one-year expired-ID boundary and credible-witness requirements.
articles.h1: Identity Decisions Beyond a Familiar Signature
articles.lede: A recognizable signature may raise confidence without satisfying the legal identification process. Work through the applicable identity route for the actual appearance.

sections.heading: Read the credential rule carefully
sections.body: A Santa Fe customer produces a driver's license that expired fourteen months ago. New Mexico's statutory listed-credential allowance extends only to credentials current or expired no more than one year before the act. A different state's longer allowance does not govern this transaction. Review the credential category as well as the expiration date. Other government identification must meet the statutory signature-or-photograph and satisfactory-identification conditions.

sections.heading: Personal knowledge has substance
sections.body: Personal knowledge arises from dealings sufficient to provide reasonable certainty about identity. An email address, account profile, or signature that resembles an old document does not by itself establish those dealings. If personal knowledge does not exist, evaluate the appropriate satisfactory-evidence route. The statute also permits requiring additional information or credentials when necessary to assure identity. A complete certificate starts with a supportable identification decision.

sections.heading: Use the credible-witness conditions
sections.body: A credible witness does more than introduce the principal. The statute requires the witness to be unrelated and unaffected by the transaction, personally known to the officer, and identified by the prescribed credential, with identity verified through an oath or affirmation. Check each requirement before treating the witness as satisfactory evidence. A willing stranger or an interested participant does not become qualified solely by offering a confident statement.

sections.heading: Remote identity adds technology rules
sections.body: For a remote appearance, the rules address credential analysis, knowledge-based authentication, and real-time visual comparison when the prescribed proofing route applies. A remote credible witness may appear through technology if all three participants can communicate simultaneously and the witness route otherwise satisfies the statute. Authentication of an electronic signature alone does not replace the principal's audiovisual appearance or the required identity determination.

faqs.q: Is a credential expired two years acceptable under the listed-ID window?
faqs.a: No. The New Mexico statutory window is no more than one year.

faqs.q: Can the officer identify a remote signer solely from an electronic-signature check?
faqs.a: No. The rule expressly rejects that substitute for compliant identification and audiovisual appearance.

articles.keyword: New Mexico employer notary journal stamp
articles.intent: Learn how New Mexico rules apply to a concrete notarial workflow
articles.title: Working as a Notary Inside a New Mexico Business
articles.description: Manage employer requests, journal custody, fee ceilings, and personal conflicts.
articles.h1: Working as a Notary Inside a New Mexico Business
articles.lede: An employer may organize appointments and purchase supplies while the officer remains responsible for the acts and official tools.

sections.heading: Separate scheduling from judgment
sections.body: An Albuquerque office manager can arrange the signing room, but the officer still determines whether the required appearance, identity, declaration, and certificate conditions are met. A supervisor's instruction to finish an incomplete record does not remove the handbook's prohibition. If knowing and voluntary action or capacity is doubtful, assess the circumstances under the refusal provisions. The statute also prohibits discriminatory performance or refusal.

sections.heading: Check direct personal interests
sections.body: The conflict rule addresses a record to which the officer, the officer's spouse, or domestic partner is a party or in which one has a direct beneficial interest. An employer's urgency does not remove that restriction. Identify the actual parties and benefits before proceeding. Where the personal conflict exists, arrange a different qualified officer rather than treating a manager's approval as a cure. The statute makes an act in violation voidable.

sections.heading: Keep custody after employment ends
sections.body: The journal remains under the officer's secure control. Statutory permission for a former employer to receive clearly marked copies of relevant entries does not give the employer the original journal. When an employee leaves, plan lawful retention or transfer and document the custody location. The required ten-year retention period continues after the officer changes jobs or stops working as a notary.

sections.heading: Protect credentials and fee limits
sections.body: A RON employer must not allow another worker to use the officer's electronic signature or stamp. Keep those credentials under the officer's sole control and access. Employers also remain subject to the applicable maximum notarial fees. For travel compensation, agree in advance and disclose that the charge is separate and is not mandated by law. A company's internal invoice policy does not override those requirements.

sources.title: SOS Handbook, Prohibited Acts and Fees

faqs.q: May the employer keep the original journal because it bought the book?
faqs.a: The officer keeps the required custody or makes an authorized transfer. Permitted employer copies must be clearly marked.

faqs.q: May a coworker use the officer's RON login?
faqs.a: No. The signature and official stamp remain under the officer's sole control and access.
