articles.intent: Learn how New Mexico rules apply to a concrete notarial workflow
articles.title: Comparing Copies and Electronic Printouts
articles.description: Evaluate eligible originals, comparison methods, certificate language, and the ordinary copy-fee formula.
articles.lede: Copy certification is an accuracy determination made through the authorized procedure. Start with the kind of original and the officer's ability to compare it.

sections.heading: Identify the source record
sections.body: At a Rio Rancho appointment, a customer asks for certified copies of a private letter and a birth certificate. The handbook's copy-certification instruction excludes vital records, public records, and publicly recordable documents. The birth certificate belongs with the appropriate official custodian. The private letter can be evaluated under the ordinary procedure if the officer has the original and can make the required accuracy determination.

sections.heading: Compare the complete reproduction
sections.body: The administrative rule permits making or supervising the copy or reviewing the original and copy. Check completeness across all pages, attachments, and relevant content. A customer's assurance that the document was scanned correctly does not make the officer's comparison unnecessary. The certificate should accurately describe the original and reproduction. The handbook separately prohibits certifying or authenticating a photograph, so an image's presence does not create a general photographic-authentication power.

sections.heading: Electronic records can produce certified tangible copies
sections.body: Current statute authorizes certifying that a tangible copy is an accurate copy of an electronic record. The remote rule treats the properly certified tangible copy as an original record and requires the applicable short-form copy certificate. A platform's print command does not itself provide that certificate or the officer's accuracy determination. Verify the electronic source and complete the applicable certification before describing the paper's status.

sections.heading: Apply the copy fee formula
sections.body: The ordinary copy-certification provision uses fifty cents per page with a minimum total charge of five dollars. A small eligible copy therefore does not require charging only a fraction of a dollar, while a larger copy uses the page formula. Do not convert that provision into five dollars for every page. Other notarial acts and any separately agreed travel charge have their own rules, so make the invoice describe what was actually performed.

sources.title: SOS Handbook, Copy Certifications and Fees

faqs.q: Can a customer waive the vital-record restriction?
faqs.a: Customer permission does not expand the handbook's copy-certification scope.

faqs.q: Does every printout from a RON platform count as a certified original?
faqs.a: The remote rule requires a certified tangible copy and the appropriate copy certificate.

articles.title: Building a Journal That Survives Daily Work
articles.description: Record contemporaneous acts, control mixed paper and electronic journals, and prepare recoverable electronic storage.
articles.h1: Building a Journal That Survives Daily Work
articles.lede: A journal becomes reliable through the way entries are created and protected throughout daily practice.

sections.heading: Record the event when it occurs
sections.body: A busy Farmington officer should make each journal entry contemporaneously and sequentially. The statutory fields include the date and time, description of the record and act, the full names and addresses of the individuals, identification information or the personal-knowledge statement, and the fee if any. An end-of-week reconstruction from memory risks omissions in both chronology and substance. Completing the certificate does not complete the separate journal duty.

sections.heading: Choose lawful formats for the work
sections.body: A tangible journal must be durable, bound, and numbered. An electronic journal must be permanent and tamper-evident. The amended statute permits a paper journal for tangible records and an electronic journal for electronic records. That permission does not remove chronological recording and required entry details. Determine where each type of act will be recorded before offering a mix of traditional and electronic services.

sections.heading: Plan recovery and production
sections.body: The administrative rule requires an electronic journal to be recoverable after hardware or software failure. It must also support the required PDF production and transfer capabilities. A convenient editable file without tamper evidence, recovery, or appropriate export support does not establish compliance. Ask a provider how those functions operate and preserve a workable recovery arrangement before a device failure makes the journal unavailable.

sections.heading: Add the remote provider detail
sections.body: A RON journal includes the name of the remote system provider used for each act in addition to the statutory fields. That entry is separate from saving the audiovisual recording. Keep the journal secure under the officer's control and preserve permitted employer copies as clearly marked copies. Retention continues for ten years after the last recorded act, so everyday format decisions also affect long-term access.

faqs.q: Can the officer keep paper for tangible acts and electronic entries for electronic acts?
faqs.a: The amended statute permits those respective formats, subject to the journal requirements.

faqs.q: Does a recording replace the RON journal entry?
faqs.a: No. The journal requires its own entry, including the provider name.

articles.title: Handling Loss and the End of a Notary Practice
articles.description: Address missing journals and devices, continuing retention, and lawful disposition after cessation or death.
articles.h1: Handling Loss and the End of a Notary Practice
articles.lede: The last appointment and the last day of a commission do not end every recordkeeping responsibility.

sections.heading: Recognize unavailable records promptly
sections.body: A notary discovers a missing journal after a move. The statute and current journal rule require prompt SOS notice on the prescribed form when a journal is lost or stolen. Prompt notice also applies to a lost or stolen stamping device. A planned purchase or an ongoing search does not eliminate the reporting duty. Review the current SOS reporting process as soon as the loss or theft is discovered.

sections.heading: Use recovery without postponing responsibility
sections.body: An electronic journal may become inaccessible even when the laptop remains in the officer's possession. The electronic-journal rule requires recovery capability after hardware or software failure. Activate that arrangement and secure remaining files and credentials while resolving the failure. If the journal has been lost or stolen, follow the prompt-notice requirement as well. A broken device on the desk does not supply accessible entries or the required recovery capability.

sections.heading: Close the practice deliberately
sections.body: After resignation or suspension, the amended journal statute requires continued retention and information about the journal's location. Keep the journal for the required period or use an authorized transfer. A transfer to the state records officer requires SOS notice within thirty days on the prescribed form. Stamping-device cessation rules also require rendering the device unusable in the applicable circumstances, including expiration or revocation.

sections.heading: Plan for death or incapacity
sections.body: A personal representative, guardian, or other person knowingly possessing the journal has statutory disposition duties after death or adjudicated incompetence. Use the authorized recipient route rather than discarding the journal with ordinary office papers. RON recordings have their own rule permitting retention, repository transfer, or delivery to SOS in an accessible open format. Written custody instructions should distinguish journals, stamping devices, and recordings.

faqs.q: Does an expired commission end journal retention?
faqs.a: No. The retention and authorized-disposition duties continue.

faqs.q: Is owning the failed storage device enough?
faqs.a: No. Electronic journal recovery and availability requirements concern the records themselves.

articles.intent: Apply New Mexico duties to an operational scenario
articles.title: Understanding the Remote Identity-Proofing Sequence
articles.description: Connect credential analysis, KBA standards, visual comparison, and the credible-witness route.
articles.lede: A remote account and an electronic signature do not complete the identification decision. New Mexico prescribes identity checks within the audiovisual appearance.

sections.heading: Start with the applicable route
sections.body: The remote officer verifies identity at the start of the online session. Where the officer does not personally know the individual and uses the prescribed proofing route, the rule requires two different types of identity proofing. Credential analysis, successful knowledge-based authentication, and live visual comparison work together. Familiarity with the person's signature or an electronic-signature verification process alone does not satisfy the remote identification rule.

sections.heading: Analyze the actual credential
sections.body: Credential analysis uses automated processes and appropriate technologies to test authenticity, including visual, physical, or cryptographic security features. It also uses issuing or authoritative source information as available and consistent with sound commercial practices. The system must permit a real-time comparison of the credential information and photograph with the individual appearing. A provider that merely reads a printed name has omitted important parts of the analysis.

sections.heading: Apply KBA specifications precisely
sections.body: The knowledge-based quiz has at least five questions and at least five choices per question. At least eighty percent must be answered correctly within two minutes. Following two failed attempts, no retake is allowed within twenty-four hours. A retake replaces at least forty percent of the prior questions. The officer must not be able to see or record the questions or answers. These are principal-identification specifications, separate from the notary licensing examination.

sections.heading: Preserve the witness and refusal boundaries
sections.body: The rule also recognizes the statutory credible-witness route, including its personal-knowledge and satisfactory-evidence conditions. A remotely located credible witness must be able to communicate simultaneously with the officer and principal. If the officer ultimately cannot verify identity in compliance with the rules, the officer must refuse completion. A signed customer waiver cannot replace the missing identification.

faqs.q: Can the officer coach the principal through KBA?
faqs.a: No. The officer must not be able to see or record the KBA questions or answers.

faqs.q: Is the two-minute KBA limit the licensing-exam time?
faqs.a: The rule's two-minute limit applies to the principal's identity quiz. It does not establish the licensing examination duration.

articles.title: Managing a Remote Session When Conditions Change
articles.description: Respond to interrupted feeds, insecure communication, coercion concerns, and failed electronic attachment.
articles.h1: Managing a Remote Session When Conditions Change
articles.lede: A RON session remains conditional on compliant communication and execution until the act is complete.

sections.heading: Observe the person and surroundings
sections.body: During a session from a New Mexico office, the officer notices a principal looking repeatedly toward someone outside the camera frame. The rule permits observing signs of nervousness, fear, hesitation, or discomfort and the behavior of others in the room. The officer can request a private conversation and ask directly about free will. Reasonable grounds to believe coercion or undue influence is present support refusing the act.

sections.heading: Restart after a broken process
sections.body: The technology must provide synchronous audiovisual feeds with sufficient clarity for the officer and principal to see and speak with each other. If either participant exits before completion, the audiovisual feed is interrupted, or quality becomes compromised, the officer stops and restarts from the beginning. A few earlier minutes of clear communication do not permit skipping the restart after a disqualifying interruption.

sections.heading: Require accessible and secure communication
sections.body: Communication technology includes accessibility accommodations for individuals with vision, hearing, or speech impairments. It also needs reasonable security against unauthorized access to the live feeds, identity-proofing methods, and electronic record. If the officer becomes aware that the communication technology is insecure, the officer must refuse completion. Customer consent to an exposed session does not remove the prescribed security duty.

sections.heading: Finish only with valid attachment
sections.body: The principal's signature must be attachable to the electronic record. The officer must also be able to attach the electronic stamp through technology that makes later modification evident. Failure of either capability requires refusal to complete the act. When all requirements are met, complete the electronic certificate with the required communication-technology disclosure. A large stamp image cannot compensate for failed tamper-evident attachment.

faqs.q: Can the officer resume at the final stamp step after an early exit?
faqs.a: The rule requires restarting the RON process from the beginning.

faqs.q: Must the officer complete an insecure session if the customer prepaid?
faqs.a: No. Awareness of insecure communication requires refusing completion.

articles.intent: Apply New Mexico duties to an operational scenario
articles.title: Evaluating a Remote Platform Through Its Duties
articles.description: Check active approval, digital credentials, provider notices, and long-term recording arrangements.
articles.h1: Evaluating a Remote Platform Through Its Duties
articles.lede: A platform's marketing page cannot answer every compliance question. Review the officer's per-act duties and the provider's operating requirements.

sections.heading: Verify approval for every act
sections.body: A New Mexico remote officer verifies that the system provider has active SOS status before using the system for each remote notarization. Initial approval at enrollment does not settle every later session. Notify SOS on the prescribed form when adopting a new provider. Provider approval also does not imply state endorsement of premium products. Claims that SOS endorses, recommends, or mandates a provider's services are a listed ground for termination of provider approval.

sections.heading: Protect the officer's digital identity
sections.body: The selected technology must provide independently verifiable, tamper-evident attachment and a valid third-party PKI digital certificate compliant with X.509 or higher. The officer may not act with an expired, revoked, invalid, or unauthenticatable certificate. The electronic signature and official stamp remain under the officer's sole control and access. An employer cannot authorize coworkers to use the officer's credentials during a shift change.

sections.heading: Examine the recording arrangement
sections.body: Recordings must be protected against unauthorized access, stored in an open file format, and exclude images of the record being notarized. The statute supplies the recording-retention period, while the repository rule addresses storage and exit arrangements. A written repository contract must support continued compliance after termination and the specified control, access to copies, or secure return of recordings. Ask how export and custody work before canceling an account.

sections.heading: Understand provider changes and complaints
sections.body: A provider must seek approval and notify its New Mexico officers at least thirty days before substantial system changes or feature enhancements. Information changes and security breaches have their own notification duties. A complaint to SOS identifies a specific RULONA or rule violation. Active status can be terminated for listed failures, including certain breaches, prohibited endorsement claims, and failure to cooperate with an investigation within the required period.

faqs.q: Does state approval mean SOS recommends a premium package?
faqs.a: No. Representing SOS endorsement or mandated use is itself a termination ground.

faqs.q: Can canceling the platform end recording retention?
faqs.a: No. The repository arrangement must support the continuing retention requirements.

articles.title: Using Automatic Notarial Authority in the Correct Role
articles.description: Distinguish automatic officers, role-specific stamps, official duties, and separate remote authorization.
articles.h1: Using Automatic Notarial Authority in the Correct Role
articles.lede: New Mexico recognizes specified notarial officers through their public or professional role. That route still carries concrete preparation and performance duties.

sections.heading: Identify the authority actually used
sections.body: The amended statute recognizes specified judicial officers, SOS or designated full-time staff within official duties, county clerks and deputies within official duties, and New Mexico licensed attorneys. The exact role determines the applicable authority and stamp identifiers. A county employee should establish whether the requested act falls within the employee's qualifying office and duties rather than treating every government position as automatic notarial authority.

sections.heading: Complete the current preparation duties
sections.body: Automatic notarial officers must complete the required learning and register their official stamp before performing acts. Historical implementation periods in the 2023 amendments do not create a continuing exemption in 2026. The automatic route does not require the ordinary commissioning application fee described for commissioned notaries. Separate authority may be relevant when a qualifying nonattorney official wants to perform acts outside official duties.

sections.heading: Order the role-specific stamp
sections.body: The automatic officer uses the required Notarial Officer and State of New Mexico wording and the current official-seal requirements. Attorney stamps include the state bar identifier. Judicial stamps identify the judicial district or area served. County-clerk stamps use the applicable county identifier. Use the current enacted distinction when reviewing a design, because a generalized web checklist can obscure the difference between judicial and county-clerk roles.

sections.heading: Apply separately for remote work
sections.body: Automatic authority for traditional acts does not itself authorize RON. A noncommissioned notarial officer who wants remote authority follows the SOS authorization application procedure and, after approval, complies with the remote rules and applicable statutes. The officer still needs a compliant system, electronic-stamp submission, required learning, secure credentials, and compliant record preservation. The role supplies the source of ordinary authority without removing the remote safeguards.

faqs.q: Does a New Mexico law license itself authorize immediate RON?
faqs.a: An attorney seeking RON must follow the separate authorization procedure.

faqs.q: Does the old implementation grace period excuse a new officer in 2026?
faqs.a: No. The historical transition does not remove the current training and stamp requirements.
